newsitem.title: UK: ACPC mulls export quotas with price triggers.
newsitem.headline: ACPC mulls export quotas with price triggers.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) is proposing to re-introduce an export quota programme with a trigger price mechanism from May, a delegate from Costa Rica said on Thursday.
Ricardo Seevers, president of the Costa Rican coffee exporters' group Ecafe, said that Colombia and El Salvador had voiced support for the ACPC secretariat's proposal.
"The idea is to put trigger prices in export quotas so we can automatically cut or release coffee into the market," Seevers told reporters after a morning session of the ACPC technical group.
"That's something that we are going to discuss today."

Seevers said the proposed scheme could be similar to the market interventions by International Coffee Organization (ICO) before the ACPC was set up, although there were no plans of keeping buffer stocks.
Different price triggers would be applied to robusta and arabica types of coffee, he said.
"The proposal is from the ACPC along with Colombia, El Salvador and Costa Rica," he said, adding that El Salvador and Costa Rica were under pressure from their growers to sell more coffee.
The technical group, which gathered on Thursday to consider high world prices and their impact on consumption cannot make any decisions.
But the proposal would be presented to the ACPC Council meeting in May.
